articles.full_text:
Kerala rain: IMD issues red alert in 3 districts tomorrow
Thiruvananthapuram: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red alert in three districts tomorrow, warning of the possibility of very heavy rainfall at isolated places. They include Malappuram, Kozhikode, and Wayanad. Thiruvananthapuram, Kollam, Alappuzha, and Kasaragod have been issued a yellow alert for tomorrow. The remaining districts have been placed under an orange alert. The alert is expected to continue till Monday.
As of today, an orange alert has been issued for Thrissur, Palakkad, Malappuram, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur, and Kasaragod. The remaining seven districts have been issued a yellow alert.
Squally weather with wind speeds of 35-45 kmph gusting to 55 kmph is likely to prevail along the coast. Fishermen have been advised to not venture into the sea during this period.
Rain and thunderstorms are expected to continue across the state, with the possibility of lightning and gusty winds. Heavy downpours could lead to waterlogging, traffic disruptions, falling trees and damage to vulnerable structures. Landslides and mudslides are also possible in hilly areas.
Residents, particularly those in landslide-prone regions, have been advised to remain vigilant and follow instructions issued by the authorities. People should exercise caution during thunderstorms and avoid venturing into rivers and other water bodies during heavy rain.

Thiruvananthapuram [Kerala]: In Keralam, rain alerts have been issued for all 14 districts. Akashvani’s Thiruvananthapuram Correspondent reports that ten districts in Keralam are under orange alert today, indicating isolated very heavy rainfall. The remaining four districts are under yellow alert, predicting isolated heavy rainfall. Lakshadweep is also under orange alert today.
Twelve districts in Keralam will be under orange alert on Sunday. The intensity of rainfall is likely to decrease on Monday, though yellow alert will remain in force across all 14 districts. Isolated heavy rainfall has been reported from several places in Keralam and Lakshadweep since early morning.
